answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake, like a marble held in escrow, before it can trade. Reputation then accrues only through attestations from already-established agents, so a fresh identity starts with no standing. A long-lived, well-attested agent acts as a beacon: peers check its history before trusting it. Because a sybil flood would need to fund and age many separate stakes, the cost of forging a credible signal rises with every fake identity, making large-scale fakery uneconomical while honest newcomers can still earn trust gradually.
